newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LASORDA, DOING WELL, IS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LASORDA, DOING WELL, IS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL.

text.p: Former Los Angeles Dodger manager Tommy Lasorda left the hospital on Sunday in good condition after having a second heart operation in nearly four months.
"He's doing extremely well. The doctors don't anticipate anymore complications," said Tara Igoe, a spokeswoman for Centinela Hospital Medical Centre.
Lasorda, 69, walked out of the hospital this afternoon, heading for a party for his granddaughter's first birthday, she said.

Lasorda told reporters he had watched the Dodgers get knocked out of baseball's National League playoff series on Saturday, losing 5-to-2 to the Atlanta Braves. He said the team's hitting was off but was still satisified with its performance.
He said he had no favourite of the teams advancing in the playoffs. "May the best team win," he said.
Lasorda was admitted to Centinela on Friday for a second angioplasty operation to clear a blocked artery. He underwent similar surgery on June 26, but tests showed the artery had clogged again.

His cardiologist, Dr. Anthony Reid said 25 to 30 percent of all patients who undergo angioplasty -- in which a balloon-like catheter is inserted into the artery then inflated to remove blockage -- return for a second procedure within one year.
Lasorda retired in July after nearly 20 years as the Dodgers' manager. He spent 47 years with the Dodgers as a player, scout, coach and, beginning in 1976, as manager.

He led the team to two World Series championships and won a reputation as one of baseball's most colourful characters. He was voted National League Manager of the Year in 1977, '81 and '88. Upon his retirement, he was named team vice president.
